note:
What the DDK delivers and what it keeps closed. Everything else about the delivery -- which libraries the roots need, how each compiles and links, which half each belongs to, what each is called -- is read from the build, and held to the last release by lock/. This file is the part the build cannot know: it says what MTK are given, not how anything is built.

Patterns are GN labels without a toolchain: //dir:name names one target, //dir:* every target in that directory, //dir/* every target under it. Where binary and source both match, the more specific pattern wins.
layout_reason: Where each part sits in output/, and so in src/hypervisor/ on MTK's side: the repo manifest provisions each part one level down, at the name of its Gerrit project -- yocto/src/hypervisor/libddk/aries_v1, grt_ddk/garnet, mtk_ddk/aries_v1. output/ is laid out the same so the release produces what the manifest checks out. The halves still build beside each other: the recipe fetches each part flat into WORKDIR, where a half finds the component as ../libddk.
mirror_reason: Where a half's mirror starts when there is no last release to continue from: a date, or a garnet revision. Everything before it is already on MTK's side, imported whole -- release 20260917-8919f813477f, built from the tree of this date -- so replaying it again would only make a history nobody deploys. Move it forward when the deployed base moves.
deploy_reason: Where deploy_delivery.py pushes each part: the Gerrit the yocto layers live on, the project is prefix/ + the part's layout path, on this branch, under this topic. The CR and ONES ids of what is pushed come from the commits themselves, not from here.
deliver_reason: The drivers the platform ships, the VMM and the programs beside it. The two littlefs libraries are delivered in their own right: nothing delivered links them, and a consumer builds filesystems against them.
exclude_reason: Built by the product and not part of what a board ships: the QEMU board driver, an I2C echo test driver, and the GPIO demo program beside the MT8676 GPIO driver. Tests need no pattern: a target GN marks testonly is never delivered.
binary_reason: Zircon is closed. Third-party code arrives compiled unless source says otherwise. blk_crypto and blk_retry are GRT's own block encryption and retry, private to GRT. Generated code -- FIDL and protobuf bindings -- is always delivered compiled and needs no pattern here.
source_reason: littlefs is delivered as source so the filesystem can be built against the DDK.
